title: Enriched Seawater for Cyanobacterial Culture
author: Rômulo Pereira de Jesus
materials: Seawater should not be collected following rainfall events, as precipitation promotes sediment resuspension, increases the load of organic matter and suspended particles, and introduces continental contaminants such as sewage, soil, and excess nutrients. These factors significantly alter seawater quality and may compromise the stability of the culture medium. Recommendation: Seawater collection should be carried out only after at least 1–2 consecutive weeks of dry and sunny weather , ensuring greater physicochemical stability of the seawater. Select flasks ranging from 1 to 5 liters according to the number of cultures required. The flasks must be cleaned with Extran and rinsed thoroughly with distilled water. Label each flask with the internal code used to identify the cyanobacteria culture. It is recommended to use thermoresistant labels; otherwise, they may be damaged during autoclaving. Avoid selecting any non-thermoresistant material for flasks.

steps.title: Collect surface seawater
steps.instruction: Collect surface seawater near the shoreline, avoiding areas with strong sediment resuspension or visible organic matter, using clean glass or appropriate plastic containers; rinse each container with seawater itself five consecutive times, then fill the container while keeping it facing against the current to prevent sand entry, and seal the container immediately after collection.

substeps.instruction: Rinse container with seawater five times
Collect required volume of surface water, container facing upstream

steps.title: Vacuum‑filter seawater
steps.instruction: Immediately upon arrival at the laboratory, vacuum‑filter the collected seawater using a Kitasato flask, Büchner funnel and standard laboratory filter paper; filter in small portions, replace the filter after every few filtrations to maintain flow rate, and transfer measured volumes (1 L) into cleaned culture flasks using a 1‑liter graduated cylinder.

substeps.instruction: Set up Kitasato flask, Büchner funnel and filter paper
Measure 1 L portions with graduated cylinder and transfer to cleaned flasks

steps.title: Supplement filtered seawater
steps.instruction: For each litre of filtered seawater add 1 mL sodium nitrate (NaNO₃), 1 mL sodium dihydrogen phosphate monohydrate (NaH₂PO₄·H₂O), and 0.5 mL trace‑metal solution; mix the medium carefully after each addition.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL trace‑metal solution per litre

steps.title: Autoclave the medium
steps.instruction: Sterilize the supplemented seawater by autoclaving; adjust the autoclave time according to the volume of solution in each container, as the required time may vary with volume.

steps.title: Cool autoclaved medium
steps.instruction: Remove the autoclaved containers from the autoclave and allow the medium to cool naturally on the laboratory bench without any external interference.

steps.title: Add vitamin mix and inoculate
steps.instruction: When the medium has cooled to room temperature, add the vitamin mix at a ratio of 1 mL per litre (heat‑sensitive components), then inoculate with the cyanobacterial culture.
